status: PROPOSED by Claude from eval/rule_cards.json includes/excludes - pending user review. straight_back_leg #30 is carried over from eval/labels_straight_back_leg_v6.json.

chunks.text: Failing to lower the chest completely to the floor reduces the total work required of the upper body, limiting potential strength and muscle development.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card consequences: smaller range, less muscle stimulus.

chunks.text: Stopping far above the ground in a partial push-up prevents the chest muscles from working to their full potential.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card consequences: less muscle stimulus.

chunks.text: Not achieving adequate range of motion limits chest stretch and development.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card consequences: smaller range, less muscle stimulus.

chunks.text: Switching to a full range of motion where the chest reaches the ground can reduce push-up repetition performance by approximately 60%, dropping rep output from 100 down to 40.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: A3, kept tagged by the user. Bottom-only (no lockout), so in scope; it explains why people shorten reps (more reps), not the mechanism. Risk: a generator could read it as 'partial reps let you do more'.

chunks.text: Full range of motion in a push-up requires descending until the elbows reach an angle of 90 degrees or less.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: how low a push-up should go (elbows about 90 degrees).

chunks.text: In a study of active females, 45% of participants passed the Trunk Stability Push-Up (TSPU) post-intervention, with many of those who failed only able to rise one to two inches from the floor.
chunks.label: irrelevant
chunks.reason: TSPU test result: failing to press up off the floor (stuck at the bottom), the opposite of stopping well above it. Debatable as 'incomplete rep from weakness'.

chunks.text: The increased force in the down position of a push-up is due to the whole-body center of mass being located further from the point of contact with the floor, which results in greater torque.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Why the bottom is the hard part, i.e. supports the card cause 'too weak to press from the bottom'. Does not name shallow reps.

chunks.text: Performing partial reps by only bending the elbows slightly and stopping far above the ground.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: shallow repetitions that stop well above the floor (close to anchor r1).

chunks.text: Performing partial repetitions where the chest does not lower close to the floor.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: shallow repetitions.

chunks.text: Performing a short-range push-up by lowering down only far enough to partially bend the elbows.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: shallow repetitions. (Not the 'go half-way down and hold' item.)

chunks.text: Failing to complete the push-up by only rising one to two inches from the floor due to insufficient upper body strength.
chunks.label: irrelevant
chunks.reason: Same TSPU context as #6: cannot press up from the floor, not a shallow descent. Debatable (incomplete rep, weakness cause).

chunks.text: Perform a full range of motion by lowering until the chest nearly touches the floor, ensuring the chest leads the way down rather than the belly or chin.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: how low (chest near the floor). The 'chest leads' clause is minor.

chunks.source: Biomechanical evaluation of the push-up exercise of the upper extremities from various starting points
chunks.text: Lower the body toward the floor until achieving 90 degrees of elbow flexion, bringing the chest as close to the ground as possible before pushing up.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: elbows about 90 degrees, chest near the floor.

chunks.text: Lower the body with control until the chest approaches the floor.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: how low.

chunks.text: Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor or your elbows bend to approximately 90 degrees, whichever comes first based on mobility.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: how low.

chunks.text: Cutting depth reduces muscle growth and motor unit recruitment because muscles grow more when stretched through a full range of motion.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card consequences: small range, muscles trained over only part of their range.

chunks.text: Failing to sufficiently activate the m. gluteus maximus reduces the generation of posterior shear forces at the tibia, which otherwise potentially contribute to a reduced likelihood of knee injuries.
chunks.label: irrelevant
chunks.reason: Glute activation and tibial shear, says nothing about depth.

chunks.source: Effects of Loading Positions on Lower Limb Biomechanics During Lunge Squat in Men with Different Training Experience
chunks.text: During backward barbell lunges, novices achieved a shallower peak knee flexion with a minimal sagittal angle of -99.01 ± 10.02 degrees compared to -108.44 ± 8.33 degrees in experienced lifters.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Research on lunge depth (novices shallower).

chunks.source: Effects of Targeted Knee Flexion Angle on the Biomechanical Factors of Upward and Downward Phases during Forward Lunge
chunks.text: During a forward lunge, a shallower front knee flexion angle of 80° results in a statistically significantly higher knee extensor moment (0.980 Nm/BW) compared to 90° (0.717 Nm/BW) and 100° (0.362 Nm/BW).
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Depth comparison of the front knee (in scope), but the effect it reports does not argue for or against depth; easy to misuse.

chunks.source: Biomechanical Analysis of the Anterior Lunge During 4 External-Load Conditions
chunks.text: Lifters tend to cut lunge depth short when handling heavier external loads, failing to lower their center of mass to full depth.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Shallow lunge plus a cause (heavy load), approved as a shallow_lunge cause in prefilter review section 10.

chunks.source: Effects of Loading Positions on Lower Limb Biomechanics During Lunge Squat in Men with Different Training Experience
chunks.text: Novice lifters may perform backward lunges with shallower knee flexion compared to experienced lifters.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Shallow lunge.

chunks.source: Influence of Different Load Conditions on Lower Extremity Biomechanics during the Lunge Squat in Novice Men
chunks.text: Exhibiting small knee flexion during a lunge indicates underlying issues such as quadriceps weakness or a limited ankle dorsiflexion range.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Shallow lunge plus card cause (weak quadriceps).

chunks.text: Failing to lower the hips until the front thigh is parallel to the floor.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes / fixes: front thigh about parallel.

chunks.text: Proper lunge depth occurs when the back knee gently touches or comes very close to the ground under control.
chunks.label: wrong_fault
chunks.reason: Depth defined by the REAR knee; the card excludes 'advice about the rear knee is a different rule'. Same situation as #27, which is in both arms. If the user rules depth-via-rear-knee in scope, #24 and #27 both become relevant.

chunks.text: During the lunge, the front knee should be flexed to approximately 90 to 100 degrees as the rear knee is lowered toward the ground.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes: how deep (front knee about 90 degrees).

chunks.source: Effects of Targeted Knee Flexion Angle on the Biomechanical Factors of Upward and Downward Phases during Forward Lunge
chunks.text: The knee flexion angle of the front leg in the downward phase should be carefully managed to prevent injuries to the knee joints during forward lunge training.
chunks.label: irrelevant
chunks.reason: No direction or target depth; if anything leans to caution about going deep.

chunks.source: Trunk and Shank Position Influences Patellofemoral Joint Stress in the Lead and Trail Limbs During the Forward Lunge Exercise
chunks.text: To achieve proper depth during a lunge, descend until the trail knee is just prior to touching the ground.
chunks.label: wrong_fault
chunks.reason: Same as #24 (depth via the rear knee).

chunks.text: Projecting the body forward during a lunge due to a straight rear leg increases force on the knee joint and causes knee pain.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card includes 'pushing the body forward onto the front leg'; consequences: load shifts onto the front knee.

chunks.text: Keeping the back leg straight while attempting to lower the body during a lunge pushes the body forward.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Definition plus the 'pushing forward' include.

chunks.text: Lower the rear knee toward the ground during the descent of the lunge.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Carried over from eval/labels_straight_back_leg_v6.json #1.

chunks.source: Patellofemoral Joint Loading in Forward Lunge With Step Length and Height Variations
chunks.text: Allow the trail knee to bend until it lightly makes contact with the ground at the bottom of the lunge.
chunks.label: relevant
chunks.reason: Card fixes: cue the back knee down toward the floor. 'Lightly' keeps it off the excluded knee-slamming.
